body:
AMEND, independently, under the anti-dither identity criterion. The arithmetic roster is internally coherent and matches the controlling D2 contract, including the 1/3 and negative-floor residuals, signed overflow boundary, two-run reset, explicit gap, occurrence-scoped reverse, and PTS/DTS refusal. The separation of ExpectedDataId, derivation, review, realization, and C1 conformance also passes.

One reproducibility hole remains beyond the complete-record and typed-mutation amendments already posted by component-ledger-review: Same / Different / Refuse assertions do not freeze the actual identities produced by successful controls and lawful mutants. An implementation can hash an extra ephemeral field, omit a semantic field that no listed mutant varies, use a stable but wrong canonical preimage, or use platform-dependent rendering and still satisfy every local Same/Different relation on JVM, JS, and Native. Three locally passing suites do not prove that the three platforms minted the same coordinate.

Narrow repair: for every successful identity-bearing expected outcome, freeze the complete normalized semantic preimage and exact expected digest or public ID, computed independently of future C1. That includes canonical mapping-relation identity, support identity where asserted, final bundle/edition identity, and both relation and derivation identities in C05. Same/Different remains useful as the mutation explanation, but each JVM/JS/Native court must compare the produced exact value to the same frozen expected constant. A lawful mutation expected to change identity carries its own exact expected identity; Refuse carries no invented ID. The independent review receipt must say the reviewer recomputed those preimages and digests, not merely the numeric projections.

With the component-ledger repairs plus this exact-value court, ACCEPT. No source, implementation, public-name, dependency, or runtime authority follows.
